title: Commerce Contracts Common Definitions v0.1
description: Shared, protocol-neutral definitions reused across the commerce evidence vocabulary. Identifiers in the contracts.dagr-commerce.dev namespace are stable, repository-local, versioned identifiers only; they are not a published, registered, or upstream standard, and network resolution is neither required nor implied. All validation is offline against the files in this repository.

contract_version.title: Contract version
contract_version.description: Semantic version of the contract vocabulary an object was authored against.

identifier.title: Opaque identifier
identifier.description: A caller-scoped, non-secret identifier. Must not carry a secret, credential, or real financial account number.

timestamp.title: RFC 3339 timestamp
timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 date-time. The `date-time` format is enforced by the reference validator via a strict FormatChecker (not merely described): non-RFC3339 strings such as "not-a-timestamp" are rejected.

digest.title: Content digest
digest.description: A cryptographic digest of a native payload. Carries the digest, never the payload. The value shape is bound to the declared algorithm and encoding: hex values must be hexadecimal with the length implied by the algorithm; base64/base64url values must use the matching alphabet.

custody_disposition.title: Custody disposition
custody_disposition.description: Where the native object actually lives. This vocabulary never takes custody of, and never copies, sensitive native objects; it references them.

custody_reference.title: Custody reference
custody_reference.description: A pointer to where a native payload is held, without embedding the payload. location_hint is a non-secret opaque locator (e.g. a store key), never a bearer URL with credentials.

sensitive_material_class.title: Sensitive material class
sensitive_material_class.description: Classes of material that must never appear as a raw value in any object of this vocabulary.

redaction_marker.title: Redaction marker
redaction_marker.description: Stands in the place of sensitive native material. A redaction marker carries no raw secret: it records the class of material and how it was removed, optionally with a digest or custody reference. A `masked` marker exposes at most a short, non-reconstructable hint. The method is bound to its evidence: `digest_only` requires a `digest`, `custody_reference` requires a `custody`, and `masked` requires a `hint`.

hint.description: A short, non-reconstructable display hint (e.g. last 4 of an already-tokenized reference). Never a full secret or full PAN.

monetary_amount.title: Monetary amount (signed)
monetary_amount.description: A protocol-neutral amount that MAY carry a sign. `value` is a decimal string to avoid floating-point drift. `currency_code` is a free 3-8 char code and does not bind any specific currency, rail, or chain. Price/charge fields do NOT use this def; they use non_negative_monetary_amount so a negative price is rejected structurally.

non_negative_monetary_amount.title: Non-negative monetary amount
non_negative_monetary_amount.description: A monetary amount for a price, charge, cap, or refund total. Identical to monetary_amount except the `value` must be non-negative (no leading minus): a negative amount such as "-999.99" is rejected structurally.

subject_reference.title: Subject reference
subject_reference.description: A generic, protocol-neutral pointer to a party, object, or resource, by opaque id and optional digest. Never embeds the referenced object's sensitive contents.

protocol_native_reference.title: Protocol-native reference
protocol_native_reference.description: A projection of a protocol-native object into the shared vocabulary. It preserves the native protocol family, version, object type, a content digest, and custody/redaction status. It is a reference to the native object, not a replacement for it, and it must not be treated as, or serialized as, an ARCS receipt or any verifier verdict.

protocol_family.description: Free-text native protocol family label (e.g. the name of the originating protocol). No specific value is required or privileged by this vocabulary.

observation_state.title: Observation state
observation_state.description: The outcome vocabulary for a single path-scoped check. Deliberately excludes aggregate-verdict words (trusted, safe, compliant, verified, governed): a single check reports only what it observed on its own path.

check_observation.title: Path-scoped check observation
check_observation.description: One check on one path. Carries no aggregate verdict and makes no claim beyond the single path it names.

path.description: A path locating what was checked (e.g. a JSON Pointer or dotted field path). Scopes the observation to exactly this location.

safe_extension_key.title: Safe extension key
safe_extension_key.description: An extension property name that does not resemble a sensitive-material field name, an aggregate-verdict field, or a native-protocol/ARCS-authority field. The match is case-insensitive and boundary-aware (word boundaries are start/end of the key or an underscore/hyphen), so "pan" is rejected but "japan"/"span" are not. Rejected key families: (a) credentials — card/pan/cvv/cvc/bearer/secret/password/private_key/mandate_token/account_number/iban/routing/ssn/api_key/token; (b) aggregate verdicts — verdict/trusted/safe/compliant/verified/governed; (c) authority impersonation — object_type/envelope_kind/arcs_receipt/verifier_verdict/receipt/attestation. This prevents the extensions bucket from reintroducing, at any nesting depth, raw credentials, an aggregate verdict, or a field that impersonates native-protocol or ARCS authority.

safe_value.title: Safe extension value
safe_value.description: A value permitted inside the extensions bucket: a scalar or null, an array of safe values, or a nested safe extension object. Because a nested object is itself a safe_extension_object, sensitive-looking keys are rejected at ANY nesting depth.

safe_extension_object.title: Safe extension object
safe_extension_object.description: An object whose property names may not resemble sensitive-material field names (propertyNames) and whose values are recursively safe (additionalProperties), so sensitive material cannot be smuggled at any nesting depth.

extensions.title: Extension bucket
extensions.description: Namespaced bucket for protocol-specific or caller-specific attributes. Keeping extensions here preserves closure on the core object while allowing additive, non-authoritative data. Must not carry raw sensitive material: sensitive-looking property names are rejected structurally at any nesting depth (see safe_extension_object). Use a redaction_marker or digest instead.

object_envelope_fields.title: Common object envelope fields
object_envelope_fields.description: Fields every top-level commerce object carries so it is self-describing and versioned.
